editorial.description_en: Wet rock at mid lightness — blue by measurement, grey by impression, and a useful reminder that those come apart.
editorial.description_ja: 雨にぬれた岩のような、青みのある灰色。

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.498, C 0.040, h 244.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 雨 (ame, rain) + 岩 (iwa, rock). It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Rain Rock" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 雨岩. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — yu-dachi at ΔE00 4.6, kumori-iwa at ΔE00 6.6, fuka-moya at ΔE00 8.2. complementary is the entry nearest the opposite OKLCh hue (64°), within 22°. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
